items.caption:
The closer I get to YHWH, the more I realize that growth doesn’t always feel good.

Sometimes the pain comes from growing.

Sometimes it comes from growing apart.

And if I’m being transparent, some of what I’ve walked through over the last few years really shook my confidence.

It made me question myself in ways I hadn’t before. I replayed conversations. Wondered what I could have done differently. Questioned how people saw me and, at times, even let that affect how I saw myself.

And one of the hardest things I’m learning is that not everything needs my defense.

When you feel misunderstood, there’s such a strong urge to set the record straight. To explain your side. To confront. To demand answers. To make sure people know what really happened.

But Jesus already knows.

He saw the conversations I wasn’t in.
He saw the intentions behind the actions.
He saw what hurt.
He saw my own heart, too.
And He knows the whole story better than I ever could.

There is so much freedom in realizing I don’t have to chase down every misunderstanding or fight to control someone else’s version of me.

And slowly, I’m learning to rebuild my confidence somewhere much steadier - not in being liked, understood, included, or validated by everyone, but in knowing who I am in Christ.

I can keep walking. Keep growing. Keep asking God to refine my heart and trust Him with the rest.

Through all the twists and turns, I’m incredibly grateful for the people God has placed beside me - the ones who have loved me well, prayed for me, encouraged me, and reminded me who I am when I struggled to remember it myself.

Especially my husband, who has been my rock through all of it. 🤍

I’m still learning. Still growing. Still being humbled.

But I’m learning that whether I’m walking through the pain or celebrating the good, I’d rather be close to Jesus than understood by everyone.

He saw it.

And that’s enough for me. 🩷🙏

#YHWH #christianmom #JesusisLord❤️

I used one layer of 1/16” acrylic and one layer of 1/8” acrylic, allowing the background layer color to show through the negative space of the top layer 😍🙌

items.transcript: School is almost here, so let's engrave some pencils. I made my own engraving pencil jig out of cardboard and featured it in a blog post for you to download. This is going to help keep my pencils still for their new engravings. I came up with some silly sayings to put on our kids' pencils. You can also put things like return to Mrs. So-and-so or just put your child's name too. Once I'm done, I just like to wipe off the residue with rubbing alcohol on a cloth and we're all set. This is one of the first laser projects I ever tried when I was new to laser crafts, so I know you're going to love trying this one out too. It is very beginner friendly. This would make such a great student or teacher gift and is easy to crank out in 20 minutes or less, jig and all. Follow for more laser crafts and ideas.
